predecessors.note: Nabhani page: "The Seljuks were expelled in 1154, when the Nabhani dynasty came to power." The page does not name the Seljuks of Kirman; Cliopatria's Great Seljuk shapes do not reach Oman.

land.text: the interior of Oman: "In 1624 Nasir bin Murshid of the Ya'Aruba took over control of Oman"

successors.note: Cliopatria's Yarubid dynasty starts in 1626; the Ya'rubid page: "first Imam of the Yaruba dynasty, elected in 1624", capital Nizwa; Rustaq, Nakhal, Julfar (1633) and Sohar (1643) followed. After 1624 the Nabhanis were tamimahs of the Banu Riyam and princes of Jebel Akhdar until 1956 (Nabhani page).

capitals.name: Bahla
capitals.note: Page: the Nabhan "came to make their capital at Bahla", but the seat of power "fluctuated" among Nizwa, Bahla and Maqniyat; no years are given for the moves.

correction.text: the Oman shape for 1169-1176 (and from 1154): the interior of Oman under the Nabhani muluk

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's only Nabhani shape, 212.6 k km2 for 1169-1176 at 42.2-49.5 E, 12.6-18.6 N, lies in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, but the Nabhani page gives "Country: Oman (historical)", founded 1154, dissolved 1624. The shape matches the Mahdids of Zabid (1158-1174, mahdids dossier), whose Cliopatria row sits in Oman: the two rows' Names are swapped. The Oman shape is used instead, from the dynasty's birth in 1154 (new keyframe nabhani-dynasty_1154). Fix fx-31 (F182): checked, kept. The correction ({'cliopatria': 'Mahdids', 'year': 1169}) resolves to the Oman shape (346 cells at 55.6-59.8 E, 21.4-26.3 N), not to Cliopatria's Yemen shape (the row 'Nabhani Dynasty'), and has no cell in common with the Mahdid keyframes; nabhani-dynasty_1154 (1154-1235) draws the same Oman shape. The 1169 conflict came from mahdids_1169, now corrected in the mahdids dossier. The Nabhani dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01): 'Country: Oman (historical)', 'Founded: 1154', dissolved 1624.

correction.text: the interior of Oman held by the Nabhani muluk

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1154-1235: Muhammed al-Fallah "emerged as a powerful leader in 1151 and had taken control by 1154", when "the Seljuks were expelled". The shape is the 84 k km2 Oman interior (Dakhiliyah, Dhahirah, Batinah, Sohar, Nizwa, Bahla) of Cliopatria's Mahdids row, extended back from 1169 to 1154. The page gives no area; it says the Nabhani controlled "overland frankincense and spice trade routes via Sohar, Yabrin, and onward to Bahrain, Baghdad, and Damascus" and were titled "Sultans of Sohar". The geometry is the Oman shape of Cliopatria's row named "Mahdids" (see the mahdids dossier), the only Omani geometry in the data.

The Nabhani page has the dynasty ruling on (Omar bin al Khattab 1451-1490, Omar al Sharif 1490-1500, Muhammad bin Ismail 1500-1529 in its table) and says "Nizwa and Rustaq were won back by the Ibadi Imamate" without a date, but it dates no 1475 collapse; the shrink is unverified (page budget) and may be the Ibadi imams' recovery. The geometry is the Oman shape of Cliopatria's row named "Mahdids" (see the mahdids dossier), the only Omani geometry in the data.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1507-1624: Cliopatria's Mahdids row ends in 1506. The Ya'rubid page: "In 1507 the Portuguese captured the coastal city of Muscat" and "gradually extended their control along the coast up to Sohar"; the Nabhani table has a "Portuguese protectorate imposed 15 April 1515". The shape of 1502-1506 is carried to 1624 minus the Muscat coast, as a low-confidence bridge; the Ya'rubids took Nizwa, Rustaq and Nakhal from 1624.

ledger.note: 1154: the Nabhani come to power in Oman. Infobox "Founded: 1154"; Muhammed al-Fallah "emerged as a powerful leader in 1151 and had taken control by 1154"; "The Seljuks were expelled in 1154, when the Nabhani dynasty came to power". The page gives Oman, not a boundary.

ledger.counterpart: Ibadi Imamate of Oman and Kingdom of Hormuz (page undated)
ledger.note: 1475: Cliopatria's shape shrinks from 84 k to 4.4 k km2. The page dates no loss: it says only that "Nizwa and Rustaq were won back by the Ibadi Imamate" (undated) and that the coast was at one point under the Kingdom of Hormuz. Bridging step at confidence 1: page silent on year and lands.

1624: Nasir bin Murshid of the Ya'Aruba takes over Oman. Nabhani page: "In 1624 Nasir bin Murshid of the Ya'Aruba took over control of Oman"; Ya'rubid page: "was the first Imam of the Yaruba dynasty, elected in 1624", who "took the main towns as well as the forts of Rustaq and Nakhal". The Nabhani page also has Suleiman bin Mudhafar, the final ruler, "removed by the Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail (1500-29)", which conflicts with 1624.

wars.name: Ya'rubid takeover of Oman
wars.outcome: Nasir bin Murshid, elected imam in 1624, took Nizwa, Rustaq and Nakhal; Julfar was taken from the Portuguese in 1633 and the fort of Sohar in 1643.

certainty.note: An interior dynasty of towns and forts with a shifting seat; no page gives a frontier, and the coast was held at times by Hormuz and the Portuguese.

notes: Nabhani dynasty (Oman). Two pages opened (budget 1-2). CLIOPATRIA ROW SWAPPED: the row named "Nabhani Dynasty" (one shape, 1169-1176, 212 k km2) lies in Yemen and Saudi Arabia and matches the Mahdids of Zabid, whose own row ("Mahdids", 1169-1506) lies in Oman and matches this dynasty; the groups' me-08 dossiers (Zurayid) call the Nabhani row "an Omani artefact" by its name, but its geometry is Yemeni. The Yemen shape is marked wrong here; the Oman geometry of the Mahdids row is used for every new keyframe (1154-1624). The mahdids dossier carries the Zabid Mahdids (1158-1174) and marks the five Oman shapes wrong there. The Wikipedia table of rulers is unusable (al-Fallah 1406-1435, no Suleiman bin Mudhafar), so identity.rulers is omitted. The page gives the end as 1624 (infobox, Nasir bin Murshid) but also has the last ruler removed by an imam of 1500-1529; Cliopatria's Oman row ends in 1506, the Yarubid row starts in 1626. The 84 k km2 shape is Cliopatria's; the pages give no area or boundary. The 1475 step and the 1507-1624 bridge are unverified (page budget). Vassalage for the suzerains' dossiers: the Portuguese protectorate of 15 April 1515 over the Nabhani ruler Muhammad bin Ismail (Portuguese dossiers); the Nabhanis "coordinated themselves politically" with Hormuz (undated). Counterparts needing dossiers: kingdom-of-hormuz (the coast of Oman and Hormuz island, Cliopatria has no row), ibadi-imamate-of-oman (Cliopatria has Imamate of Oman only for 1913-1919). Gazetteer names needed: Bahla (not in places.jsonl).
